includedPullRequests.title: Add alarm snooze page to watch app
includedPullRequests.body:
Use case: Inspired by an idea from Justin, I'd like to be able to proactively silence Trio from the watch app. I'd like to change or stop an active snooze period from the watch app. Typical scenario: in a meeting, at the movies, or in another social setting and want to silence Trio without having to take out the phone.

This PR adds a third watch page showing the current alarm snooze state with the remaining time. Tapping it opens the same snooze options as the iPhone sheet, including ending an active snooze.

The iPhone now includes the snooze end date in the watch state and pushes an update whenever the snooze changes. The Home bell pill observes snooze changes so snoozes from the watch show up immediately.

**There's a +1 min bug** that needs to be fixed, but I'm putting it out here as a draft to get input, comments, testing, etc.

includedPullRequests.title: Mark a determination enacted only when the loop enacts it
includedPullRequests.body: When a closed loop runs while the pump is suspended, enactDetermination returns without dosing, but finalizeLoop still marked the determination as enacted. Nightscout then received the suggested temp basal and SMB as enacted even though nothing was delivered. enactDetermination now returns whether it enacted, and the determination is marked enacted only when it did. Verified with a Medtrum base simulator over Bluetooth: loops during a suspend are uploaded as not enacted, and the device status keeps the last real enactment.

includedPullRequests.title: Upload the pump status read at upload time, suspended also during a pod change
includedPullRequests.body: The device status pump status came from a file written only on pump status updates, so its timestamp was often far behind the upload. It is now read from the pump manager when the device status is uploaded. Omnipod reports delivery as active since the distant past while no pod is active, so during a pod change and after a pod fault the pump showed as not suspended. A pump that reports delivery active since before its last pump suspend, with no resume, temp basal or pump bolus after it, is now uploaded as suspended. Verified with a Medtrum base simulator over Bluetooth through a suspend and a patch change. The Omnipod path is covered by unit tests and matches the deactivation and fault handling in OmnipodKit, but has not run against a real pod.

includedPullRequests.title: Ignore manual glucose when filtering CGM readings
includedPullRequests.body:
A manual fingerstick counted as the latest CGM reading. Any CGM reading that arrived within 3.5 min after it was silently dropped as too frequent and never backfilled. Plugin CGMs that filter on `startDateToFilterNewData` (LibreTransmitter, Dexcom Share) also discarded readings older than the fingerstick, and the pump BLE heartbeat was aligned to the manual entry.

- `syncDate()`, `lastGlucoseDate()` and the backfill dedup now only consider CGM rows (`NSPredicate.cgmGlucose`)
- Debug log when readings are skipped as too frequent
- Tests for both paths; they fail without the fix

Note: the algorithm still uses manual readings as input, so a fingerstick and a CGM reading can now sit 1–2 min apart and get averaged into current BG. This already happens when a fingerstick follows a CGM reading.

includedPullRequests.title: Store the pump status in Core Data
includedPullRequests.body: Follow-up to #1697. The pump status is stored in Core Data when its basal delivery state or delivery uncertainty changes, and monitor/status.json is removed. Without a pump manager, the device status upload uses the last stored status, with the upload time as timestamp and bolusing false. A removed pump is stored as unknown and uploaded as suspended, as is Omnipod's delivery active since the distant past while no pod is active. Rows older than 90 days are purged with the other entities. Tested in the simulator with OmnipodKit against a DASH pod simulator and with MedtrumKit against a Medtrum Nano simulator, through pairing or patch activation, suspend, resume, uncertain delivery after a lost pod response, pod and patch deactivation and removing the pump. The stored states and the pump status in the uploaded device status were verified against a Nightscout server.

includedPullRequests.title: [Duo 1/5] Therapy editors: size the save bar to its container, not the screen
includedPullRequests.body:
The four therapy editors (Glucose Targets, Basal Rates, Carb Ratios, Insulin Sensitivities) size their save bar with `UIScreen.main.bounds.width`. On the iPhone Duo's closed display, the side tab bar and status bar take 84 pt of the screen width. The full-width bar then pushes the whole editor about 42 pt to the left, off the edge of the screen.

This sizes the bar's background to its container, still edge to edge, and makes the button 0.9 × its container with `containerRelativeFrame`. On every other iPhone the container is the full screen width, so nothing changes there.

![Insulin Sensitivities before and after, on iPhone Duo, iPhone SE (3rd gen) and iPhone 17 Pro](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d5574c2-6e7d-47c1-b100-c6f224f9b55d)

This doesn't change one thing that's already in upstream on every iPhone: the bar's background ends in a faint line at the tab bar (arrows below). On the Duo it runs behind the side tab bar. A separate PR could replace the background with an overlay.

![The faint line where the save bar's background ends, zoomed, on iPhone SE, iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone Duo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d03ccd00-4730-4747-99ab-c8b5295f7f94)

Tested with an Xcode 27.1 build on the simulators:
- iPhone Duo (iOS 27.1, closed): all four editors are fixed.
- iPhone SE (3rd gen) and iPhone 17 Pro (iOS 27.0): the before and after screenshots are pixel-identical.

includedPullRequests.title: [Duo 2/5] Treatments and adjustment forms: pin the list's top content margin
includedPullRequests.body: The Treatments sheet and the Add and Edit forms for overrides and temp targets ignore the top safe area with `.ignoresSafeArea(edges: .top)`, then push their `List` back down with a fixed `.padding(.top, N)`. That relies on the 35 pt top content margin iOS gives a List on iPhone. On the iPhone Duo's closed display, iOS 27.1 uses 0 instead, so the first row sits under the sheet's bar. This keeps upstream's padding and pins the list's top margin with `.contentMargins(.top, 35, for: .scrollContent)`. includedPullRequests.title: [Duo 3/5] Help sheets: pad inside the NavigationStack, not around it
includedPullRequests.body: `SettingInputHintView`, the shared help sheet behind the question-mark buttons on 31 settings screens, puts `.padding()` on its root `NavigationStack`, and so do `OverrideHelpView`, `TempTargetHelpView` and `ContactImageHelpView`. On the iPhone Duo's closed display the sheet has a trailing safe-area inset for the status bar and side tab bar. Padded from outside, the stack's content loses that inset twice. This keeps only `.padding(.vertical)` on the stack and moves the horizontal padding inside it, onto the `List` and the Got it! button, so the inset applies once.
